text.11:
LotCAD is a cross-platform 3D CAD engine built with Vulkan.
        Explore CAD modeling, visualization, and application development.
text.15: LotCAD combines 2D drafting, 3D modeling, and Vulkan visualization in a cross-platform CAD application. It can integrate with a local LLM to turn 2D floor plan images into 3D models, while its C API lets developers bring the engine into desktop and mobile apps.
text.17: Create sketches, boxes, cylinders and extruded profiles. Edit supported feature dimensions, add pockets and through-cuts, and keep changes in a native LotCAD project.
text.19: Work with lines, arcs, text, dimensions and hatches. Create projected drawing views and sections, then export supported drawing linework to PDF or PNG.
text.21: Explore assemblies, imported models and robot motion. Use the SDK examples to connect rendering and CAD commands to your own application.
text.23: Model precise parts, navigate around obstacles and connect articulated assemblies.
text.24: Concept illustration — CAD modeling, navigation and joint control.
text.26: Actual captures from the hex spacer, flange coupling and navigation demos.
text.28: A hex spacer built with extrusion, a tapped-hole cut and an external thread.
text.30: Top, front, right and isometric views, with an A-A section showing the internal hole.
text.32: A 38-part flange coupling shown midway through its exploded-view sequence.
text.34: A path planned around scene obstacles in the navigation test demo. Click a destination to move an agent through the scene.
text.37: Choose a native project for editing, a mesh format for exchange, or a drawing format for documentation. Linked examples are available to open or download; other filenames illustrate each format's use.
text.38: File formats, supported operations and examples
text.45: Native LotCAD project for objects, layers and editable modeling definitions.
text.49: Wavefront geometry for sharing meshes and curves.
text.53: Triangle mesh geometry for 3D printing and mesh exchange.
text.57: 2D drawing exchange for supported lines, circles, arcs, polylines and text.
text.61: Scene and mesh exchange. Export writes a single binary GLB file.
text.66: Static polygon meshes, materials and textures.
text.70: Point-cloud data, including point colors when present.
text.74: Volume data for extracting a surface mesh.
text.78: NIfTI volume data for extracting a surface mesh.
text.82: Drawing views, dimensions, text and linework for documents and images.
text.85: FBX import covers static geometry. PLY import reads points. PDF and PNG drawing export includes supported 2D linework and drawing views.
text.86: Browse public example models and their companion assets →
text.88: Explore practical workflows in the demo videos and build your own app with the public SDK samples.
text.90: A CAD modeling demo covering extrusion, threaded features, dimension edits, projected drawing views, a section view and PDF output.
text.93: A 38-part assembly example for exploring component placement and an exploded view.
text.96: Load the URDF robot example and control joints, the gripper and automatic motion through shared SDK demo logic.
text.99: Start with direct C API calls or embed the engine in a Qt 6 desktop interface.
text.103: Connect LotCAD to MFC, WPF or WinForms. C# samples use the native C API through P/Invoke.
text.108: Explore macOS and iOS Swift hosts, or an Android Kotlin interface connected through JNI.
text.113: Go beyond drafting with navigation, joint control and application integration.
text.115: Click a destination to move characters or vehicles through a scene. Plan paths around obstacles and update routes as movement progresses.
text.118: Connect scene objects in parent-child hierarchies. Define rotation or sliding joints, set axes and pivots, and control joint values through the interface or C API.
text.121: Embed the engine in Qt/QML, MFC, WPF, WinForms, Swift or Android hosts. Call CAD commands from C++, C# through P/Invoke, or Kotlin through JNI.
text.124: Watch LotCAD modeling and visualization demos.
text.127: Choose a destination and watch an agent move through the scene while avoiding obstacles.
text.130: Download the desktop application for Windows, macOS or Linux. Android and iOS links lead to SDK samples.
text.141: Requirements: Apple Silicon · macOS 14+; Windows 10/11 x64; Ubuntu 24.04+ x86_64. Windows and Linux require a Vulkan GPU driver.
